prompt: A Cortex-M4 telemetry board stops on the first packet after a dispatch change. Nothing was reflashed and no probe is attached: the workspace holds the board source, the build and capture tools, the record the target wrote in faults/fault-1.txt, and the matching image with symbols in faults/fault-1.elf. Work from that record and that image: decode which fault class fired and which status bits carry it, explain what the recorded faulting address can and cannot mean for this class, and resolve the stacked frame to the code that executed and the code that called it. Then decide whether the recorded instruction is the defect or where a corrupted pointer became visible, repair firmware/board.c so every packet reaches its handler, and record the triage in diagnosis.json in the shape the README specifies. The harness rebuilds your source with a fresh seed and runs it, so the published checksum must come from the repaired dispatch path executing on the target.

requirements: real Cortex-M4 target built from the workspace source with clang for thumbv7m-none-eabi and linked with ld.lld
hardware fault record captured from the running target, carrying the stacked frame plus CFSR, HFSR, MMFAR, BFAR and EXC_RETURN
matching ELF with symbols shipped next to the record it produced
diagnosis.json derived from the record and the ELF symbol table
repaired source, rebuilt with a fresh seed and executed on the target

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The diagnosis names the recorded fault class and status bits, and the image hash and MCU identity of the image that produced the record.
The stacked frame is resolved against faults/fault-1.elf, with the executed address and the calling site named from that symbol table rather than from the current source layout.
The faulting address is interpreted within what this fault class permits, and no cause is claimed from that address alone when the class carries no valid address register.
The repaired source is rebuilt with a fresh seed and run on the target, all packets reach their handler, and the published checksum matches the packets derived from that seed.

requiredEvidence: board and MCU identity, image hash, and the ELF that matches the record
raw captured record with the decoded fault class and status bits
stacked PC and LR resolved to named symbols in the matching ELF
the corrupting change identified in the source
target before/after reproduction of the dispatch path
